about: The first screen's data, written by src/data/build-field.mjs from data/; do not edit by hand. Each field dot is a group of `unit` contests at its group's median N (p is 1 in N). `per` is log10 of N ÷ population, null where the data give no population. `avg` marks a p that is an average (a state legislative class C, a chamber's average district; or like past races), never the district's own.

cases.name: South Dakota state house, district 28A
cases.src: Forecast: this site's own model, from this district's last result, whether its member ran again and the chamber's lean, fitted on earlier years only. The count: the MIT Election Data and Science Lab's Precinct-Level Returns 2024 by Individual State.
cases.role: the lowest of 641 with a district forecast

cases.name: U.S. House, California 22
cases.src: Forecast: this site's own model, built only from what was known before the election (the model's own (D2-v3), normal, calibrated to earlier years' near-ties). The count: Clerk of the House, Statistics of the Presidential and Congressional Election of November 5, 2024 (published 2025-03-10), from official sources.

pop.src: the Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2024 1-year estimates, table B01003 Total Population

cases.note: this route's back-test shows more near-even finishes than it forecast (105 against 87.5 within 1 point, 2010 to 2024), so p may be low

cases.name: President, in Nevada
cases.src: Forecast: this site's own model, built only from what was known before the election (538's national average of 2024-09-12, the last in any file reachable here (its later 2024 averages are unreadable); errors fitted to the 9 September averages of earlier cycles; the file is 538's uncorrected copy, whose bug 538 says overstated Harris's margin by 0.1 points). The count: the Federal Election Commission's official results, 2024.

pop.src: the Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program: Annual Estimates of the Resident Population of States, 2020-2024 (vintage 2024)

cases.role: the highest chance of any state

cases.name: President, for the average voter
cases.src: The chance of the average voter of 2024: each state's chance, weighted by its two-party vote, averaged over the 51 states with a chance. Forecast: this site's own model, as for each state.

pop.src: the Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program: Annual Estimates of the Resident Population of States, 2020-2024 (vintage 2024)

cases.mark: An average over the states, not one contest.
